THE INJECTION-CAMPAIGN SAMPLE, DRAWN AND WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE ANY DATA WERE
FETCHED.

The published completeness was measured by injecting carriers into 21 Class A
windows and transferring the result to the remaining 381.  This file draws the
extension of that campaign.  It is deliberately a separate, small, readable
script that writes its output once, because the one thing a reader must be able
to check is that the sample was fixed BEFORE the measurement -- not chosen
afterwards from the windows that gave a convenient answer.

DESIGN.

  * POPULATION: the 402 Class A (fine-channel, drift-searched) windows of the
    released catalogue `per_target_results_v3.99.csv`.  21 are already injected
    and are carried forward; the frame for the new draw is the other 381.

  * SAMPLING UNIT IS THE EXECUTION BLOCK, not the window.  The cost of this
    campaign is dominated by re-fetching and re-calibrating an execution
    block from the archive; once a block's calibrated measurement set exists,
    injecting every one of its Class A windows is nearly free.  So the draw is
    a stratified random sample of blocks, and EVERY Class A window of a drawn
    block enters the campaign.  This is an ordinary cluster sample and it is
    stated as one.

  * STRATA: band x array (12 m against the 7 m compact array), which are the
    two variables that are properties of the block and so can be controlled in
    a block-level draw.  Allocation is proportional to the number of Class A
    WINDOWS each stratum holds, so the campaign's window count, not its block
    count, is representative.

  * CHANNEL WIDTH, CONTROL-RING STATISTIC AND INTEGRATION LENGTH are window
    properties that vary inside a block and cannot be controlled by a
    block-level draw.  They are not controlled: they are MEASURED on the
    achieved sample and compared with the population, and that comparison is
    published.  Saying which variables were controlled and which were only
    checked is the honest version of "stratified".

  * THE ORDER IS A PRIORITY LIST OVER THE WHOLE FRAME, not a fixed set of n
    blocks.  Each block gets the key (i + 0.5) / N_s, where i is its random
    rank inside stratum s and N_s is that stratum's block count.  Any prefix of
    that list is then approximately proportionally allocated across strata, so
    attrition -- a block the archive will not deliver, a calibration that
    fails, a disk ceiling -- walks down the list without unbalancing it.  How
    far down the list we reached is reported; it is not chosen.

  * NOTHING IN THE KEY LOOKS AT THE SCIENCE.  The key is a function of the
    seed and the stratum only.  `crossing`, `disposition`, `star_snr`,
    `ctrl_max_snr`, `p_rank_*` and the line columns are not read when the
    order is built, and this file asserts that the achieved sample's crossing
    rate is consistent with the population's rather than claiming it by
    construction.

  * SEED: 180011, fixed here, never searched over.

Writes `campaign_plan_r11.json` (the priority list, with every block's
stratum, key, size and window list) and `SELECTION.md` (the same thing for a
reader).  Run once; it refuses to overwrite.
